q: The follower set (right context) of a word w in a subshift X determines its syntactic complexity. For minimal subshifts, the map w ↦ F(w) has the property that as |w| → ∞:
opts: F(w) shrinks to a single word
F(w) stabilises to F(w') for longer extensions w' of w (the future eventually determines the word's type)
exp: In an SFT, follower sets are determined by the last m symbols (where m is the memory). In general minimal subshifts, the number of distinct follower sets equals the number of states in the minimal right-resolving presentation. The follower-set complexity measures syntactic complexity.
